description: Composite two-panel figure of mixed type. (a) is a low-magnification electron micrograph of Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni steel after 70% thickness reduction in cold rolling and annealing at 900 °C for 2 min; a 10 µm scale bar is printed at lower left. The image shows a strongly banded microstructure of alternating dark and light elongated striations running broadly horizontally, overlaid with three white dashed rectangles numbered (1), (2) and (3) (large central band, upper-left banded zone, lower-right zone). At the supplied resolution no individual nanoscale particles are resolvable inside the boxes. (b) is a mechanism schematic: a deformed γ grain labelled 10–20 µm containing shear bands (black arrow) follows two routes — "Recrystallization" to 1–2 µm grains, giving "B2 precipitation at grain boundaries and edges: type 2 in Fig. a" with "B2 size: 200–1000 nm"; or "No recrystallization", giving "B2 precipitation at shear bands: type 3 in Fig. a" with "B2 size: 50–300 nm". A horizontal arrow runs from blue "Cold rolling" to red "Annealing", converting "Austenite + B2 band" into "Austenite + B2 band + B2 precipitates". The figure argues that recrystallisation state during annealing controls where B2 forms and how coarse it grows.

subfigures.description: Electron micrograph of the cold-rolled (70%) and annealed (900 °C, 2 min) Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni steel, 10 µm scale bar at bottom left. Banded dark/light striated contrast; three white dashed rectangles labelled (1) (large central band), (2) (upper-left banded area) and (3) (lower-right area). Individual nanoscale B2 particles are not resolvable at this resolution.

Schematic of B2 formation mechanism. Starting deformed γ grain (10–20 µm) with shear band branches into a 'Recrystallization' path (1–2 µm grains, B2 at grain boundaries and edges, type 2 in Fig. a, B2 size 200–1000 nm) and a 'No recrystallization' path (B2 at shear bands, type 3 in Fig. a, B2 size 50–300 nm). A bottom arrow marks cold rolling (blue) → annealing (red) with the phase assemblage changing from 'Austenite + B2 band' to 'Austenite + B2 band + B2 precipitates'.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an electron micrograph with a printed 10 µm scale bar and strongly banded, striated dark/light contrast typical of a rolled and annealed two-phase structure.
Panel (a) contains three white dashed rectangles labelled (1), (2) and (3) marking the regions of interest discussed in the caption.
The caption states the material is a Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni steel given a 70% thickness reduction in cold rolling and annealed at 900 °C for 2 min.

The caption assigns area (1) to B2 stringer bands transformed from δ-ferrite produced from the liquid, area (2) to B2 particles transformed from α precipitates at γ grain boundaries and edges, and area (3) to B2 particles transformed from α precipitates at shear bands within a γ grain.
The schematic labels the deformed γ grain width as 10–20 µm and marks a shear band inside it with a downward arrow.
In the schematic, the recrystallisation route produces B2 precipitation at grain boundaries and edges ('type 2 in Fig. a') with printed B2 size 200–1000 nm.
In the schematic, the no-recrystallisation route produces B2 precipitation at shear bands ('type 3 in Fig. a') with printed B2 size 50–300 nm, i.e. finer than the boundary-precipitated B2.
The schematic labels the recrystallised grain size as 1–2 µm, much finer than the 10–20 µm deformed γ grain.
A horizontal arrow at the bottom of the schematic spans 'Cold rolling' (blue) to 'Annealing' (red) and is annotated 'Austenite + B2 band' before and 'Austenite + B2 band + B2 precipitates' after.
No discrete B2 particles or precipitates can be individually resolved inside the dashed boxes of panel (a) at the supplied resolution; the boxes indicate location only.

The citing text states that in a Ni-alloyed Fe–15Mn–10Al–0.86C–5Ni steel the B2 phase transformed from α-ferrite is stronger than the austenite matrix and can be used to increase strength if the B2 particle size is reduced to nanoscale.
The citing text states that α-precipitates can also form along shear bands or twin boundaries, and that in duplex (δ + γ) microstructures α-ferrite forms preferentially on existing δ-ferrite.

unreadable_items: panel (a): individual B2 particles inside dashed boxes (1), (2), (3) cannot be resolved at the supplied resolution
panel (a): the exact imaging mode (SE vs BSE) is not stated in the figure
caption text for areas (1)–(3) is garbled by subscript markup (e.g. 'transformed from d ferrite', 'a precipitates', 'c grain'), so the phase symbols α/δ/γ are uncertain
